svg.text: XIAO ESP32-S3 + Wio-SX1262, SEN54, PMS5003, SHT40 · 5 V USB wall supply · top view
Nets, the same colour on every sheet
Solder the header into the XIAO only and trim the stubs flush. The Wio's edge pads over D0 to D4 carry radio
lines, a pin through both boards ties them to the button, LED, SET and SDA.
Never power the radio without its antenna. D8, D9 and D10 are the radio's SPI bus, leave them empty.
R1 and R2 are the 4.7 kΩ pull-ups the bare SEN54 needs. The Grove SHT40 brings its own 10 kΩ.
5 V fan and laser, 3.3 V logic
Firmware: Meshtastic (Bayu variant) listens on D7, drives D6 to the PMS RXD and D2 to SET, so it can sleep the fan. The Bayu firmware v5 only listens on D7 and
never drives the PMS, SET then floats high and the fan keeps running. Wire all three and the same node runs either.
PMS pins 6 (RESET), 7 and 8 stay open. The sensor pulls SET and RESET up inside, so there is no resistor on them. Logic is 3.3 V on every line, no level shifter.
Keep the I2C wires under 10 cm, Sensirion asks for it. Both sensor cases are tied to their GND pin, keep them off other metal.
SW1 and U7 are optional and only the Meshtastic build uses them, the Bayu firmware v5 reads the XIAO's own BOOT button. R3, 330 Ω, sits in series on the LED data
line on every variant. U7 runs on 3V3. The WS2812B asks for 3.5 V, but one pixel lights fine on 3.3 V and then reads the GPIO cleanly.
Power: a 5 V / 2 A USB-C wall supply. The XIAO's 5V pin is USB VBUS, the top rail carries it as +5V_USB. On the Core it goes through F1 first and becomes +5V_F.
